Generate One Synthetic Column From a Spec

Source: R/lib_synthetic.R
mksyncol.Rd

Builds one column of synthetic (made-up) data from a short specification, such as “sample these categories with these weights” or “Poisson counts with mean 25”. It is the building block of mksyncsv, which assembles a whole table from a recipe. Use synthetic columns to develop and test an analysis pipeline before, or instead of, touching restricted data.

Usage

mksyncol(spec, n, ctx = list(), basep = NULL)

Arguments

spec

A list describing the column: type and the fields listed in Details. Lists as parsed from JSON (for example values = list("a", "b")) are accepted.

n

Whole number: how many values to generate.

ctx

Named list of already-generated columns. Later columns can then reference earlier ones, as id_pattern does with a year_col. Defaults to an empty list.

basep

Optional numeric vector of per-row latent propensities in \([0, 1]\), length n, used by the "bernoulli" type to add row-level variation. Default NULL.

Value

A vector for the requested column type: character for "sample" of strings, "bernoulli" and "id_pattern", numeric or integer for "poisson" and "sequence" (and for "sample" of numbers). Its length is n, except for "id_pattern" with a year_col.

Details

The supported spec$types and the fields each reads (defaults in parentheses):

"sample" (the default type)

values, a vector or list of categories; weights (default equal), their probabilities. Drawn with replacement.

"bernoulli"

p (default 0.1), the probability of the first label; labels (default c("Yes", "No")); p_with_baserate (default 0), added as p_with_baserate * basep to give row-level variation when basep is supplied. A per-row probability above 1 behaves as 1.

"poisson"

lambda (default 1); min (default 0), a floor: draws below it are raised to it (so the result is not Poisson below the floor).

"id_pattern"

pattern (default "id-\{seq:05d\}"), in which {seq:05d} becomes a five-digit zero-padded sequence number and {year} the year; year_col, the name of a column in ctx whose values supply {year} and restart the sequence within each year. With year_col, that column must have n values. No other tokens are recognised.

"sequence"

from (default 1): from, from + 1, ....

"fitted"

fit, a dstfit result, and family (default the first-ranked converged fit): draws from that fitted distribution.

Random draws use R's random number generator, so call set.seed() first for a reproducible column. Errors: spec not a list; an unknown type; errors from sample() or rpois() on invalid weights or rates.

See also

mksyncsv.

Examples

set.seed(1)
# "sample": categorical draw, optionally weighted.
mksyncol(list(
  type = "sample", values = list("a", "b"),
  weights = list(0.7, 0.3)
), 5)
#> [1] "a" "a" "a" "b" "a"

# "bernoulli": two-label draw at probability p.
mksyncol(list(
  type = "bernoulli", p = 0.5,
  labels = list("Yes", "No")
), 5)
#> [1] "No"  "No"  "No"  "No"  "Yes"

# "poisson": counts with a floor via min.
mksyncol(list(type = "poisson", lambda = 3, min = 1), 5)
#> [1] 2 1 4 2 4

# "id_pattern": templated IDs (the {seq:05d} token is zero-padded).
mksyncol(list(
  type = "id_pattern",
  pattern = "case-{seq:05d}"
), 3)
#> [1] "case-00001" "case-00002" "case-00003"

# ... numbered within each year of an earlier column
yrs <- c(2024, 2024, 2025)
unname(mksyncol(list(type = "id_pattern",
  pattern = "{year}-{seq:05d}", year_col = "year"), 3,
  ctx = list(year = yrs)))
#> [1] "2024-00001" "2024-00002" "2025-00001"

# "fitted": draws from a distribution fitted by dstfit()
f <- dstfit(stats::rexp(100, 2), fams = "exponential", nboot = 0)
mksyncol(list(type = "fitted", fit = f), 4)
#> [1] 0.2982046 0.4023028 0.8290420 0.9676400

# "sequence": a running integer sequence from from.
mksyncol(list(type = "sequence", from = 100), 4)
#> [1] 100 101 102 103

# An unknown type errors.
try(mksyncol(list(type = "nope"), 3))
#> Error in mksyncol(list(type = "nope"), 3) : 
#>   Unknown synthetic column type: nope
